# refactor(config): split config I/O from policy and own retry defaults

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

## What

Settings files and the environment are still read the same way and give the same results, but the
code that decides what a setting means no longer reads files itself.

## Why

Configuration rules are mixed with file and directory access. That makes them hard to reuse from
anything other than the command line, and hard to test without a disk. Retry defaults also live with
business rules even though they are configurable values.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec sections: "Configuration and defaults", "Application preparation and resource lifetime".

- `src/config/load-config.ts` (`loadConfig`, `configFileFor`), `src/config/presets.ts`
  (`discoverPresets`, `presetDirectories`, `loadPreset`), `src/config/write-config.ts`
  (`updateConfigFile`) and `src/config/environment.ts` mix schemas and resolution with file reads
  and writes, directory discovery and `process.env`.
- Config keeps the schemas, default values, provider/model policy, preset-name validation,
  precedence and selection. Move file reading and writing, and preset directory discovery, to
  adapters behind narrow capabilities (functions or small port interfaces). Environment capture
  moves to the process edge. Config parses the raw values it is given. Parse each input once, at its
  edge; never copy a schema into a caller.
- `src/domain/settings.ts` exports `MAX_STEP_RETRIES = 2` and `RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5000`, and
  `runSettingsFrom` in `load-config.ts` imports them. Move both to config-owned defaults with the
  same values. Domain keeps `RunSettings` and rules such as comparing review cycles with the
  resolved cap. Do not add operator overrides (separate work), and do not let presets set run settings.
- Do not move other caps just because they are numbers. Genuine safety and stopping rules stay in domain.
- Error classes stay where they are for now; a later issue reassigns them. Keep returning the same
  `ConfigInvalid` values.

## Done when

- [ ] No file under `src/config/` imports `node:fs` or reads `process.env`
      (`grep -rnE "node:fs|process\.env" src/config --include=*.ts | grep -v spec` finds nothing).
- [ ] `src/domain/settings.ts` no longer exports the retry defaults; config supplies 2 and 5000 ms.
- [ ] Existing config, preset and environment behavior tests pass. New tests cover the moved I/O
      through fakes or temporary directories.
- [ ] The verification below passes.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/55

docs.design:
# Design

## Goal

Separate configuration policy from filesystem and process access without changing settings, precedence, errors, command behavior, or recovery. Config owns retry defaults of `2` and `5000` ms; domain continues to consume resolved `RunSettings`.

## Context

- `src/config/load-config.ts` owns the configuration schema, defaults, provider validation, warnings, required-role checks, and `runSettingsFrom`. It also reads files synchronously. An absent repository configuration produces defaults from `{}`; an explicitly selected missing file returns `ConfigInvalid`. `configFileFor` only selects a path and records whether the selection was explicit.
- `src/config/write-config.ts` reads an existing JSON object, merges supplied keys, and persists formatted JSON with `write-file-atomic`. Its deliberately permissive object schema preserves unrelated keys; it is different from the strict runtime configuration schema.
- `src/config/presets.ts` combines schemas, name validation, precedence, selection, package-relative location discovery, filesystem probing, and loading. Repository, home, XDG, then builtin precedence applies before reading winners. Broken winners never fall through. Named loading probes only the requested name; discovery reads all winners. Presets replace complete role configurations and cannot supply run settings.
- `src/config/environment.ts` already accepts raw environment values rather than reading `process.env`. Its remaining external access is `homedir()`. It owns empty-as-unset normalization, telemetry interpretation, and environment-over-saved-credential precedence.
- `src/cli/with-app.ts` captures process inputs and currently performs repository checks, environment and saved-credential loading, configuration loading, preset selection, container creation, and disposal. `src/cli/commands/presets.ts` lists presets through that preparation. `src/app/init-sandbox.ts` reads and updates configuration during initialization.
- `src/domain/settings.ts` currently owns the two retry defaults alongside `RunSettings` and genuine stopping rules. Provider/model policy and scratch naming already live in `src/config/agent-policy.ts` and `src/config/scratch-directory.ts`; preserve those boundaries.
- The application-boundaries spec assigns parsing/defaults/selection to config, external operations to adapters, process capture to the executable edge, and preparation/lifetime policy to app. The house rules additionally require one schema per owner, parsing at the input edge, narrow `Result` failures, library-backed atomic writes, and behavior tests using fakes or temporary directories. Ports may depend only on domain, so a port cannot import `JigConfig` or `Preset`.

## Chosen approach

Use pure config policy functions and small adapter-backed loading capabilities. Keep the existing construction mechanism and operation-specific preparation order.

### Configuration reads and updates

Keep `ConfigFile`, `configFileFor`, configuration schemas, validation, warnings, and resolved-setting construction in config. Export the necessary parsing operations without copying schemas into adapters. Pure path selection is not filesystem I/O and need not move.

Introduce configuration file operations under `src/adapters/config/`. A loader obtains file contents and applies config-owned parsing once before returning `Result<JigConfig, ConfigInvalid>`. Preserve the current distinction between an absent implicit repository file and an explicitly selected missing file, including existing filesystem probing behavior and diagnostic names.

Move the read/merge/write operation to this adapter area. Config retains the object-validation and merge policy; the adapter owns reads, JSON decoding at the external boundary, serialization, and `write-file-atomic` persistence. Preserve the update-specific message for malformed JSON or non-object content, unrelated keys, two-space indentation, trailing newline, and the existing behavior when the destination is absent. Do not validate update input through the strict runtime configuration schema: that would reject existing files the updater currently preserves.

Wrap only throwing library operations with `Result.try` or `Result.tryPromise`. Keep existing `ConfigInvalid` classes and messages. Do not wrap config callbacks in broad catches that could turn panics into expected failures.

### Preset discovery and selection

Split location mechanics from policy rather than relocating `presets.ts` intact. Adapters construct concrete repository/home/XDG/package locations, enumerate directories, probe entries, read files, and decode JSON. Config owns source order, the absolute-XDG selection rule, normalized-path deduplication, valid preset names, deterministic ordering, shadow removal, missing-selection diagnostics, schema validation, and whole-role application.

Use a narrow preset source capability for listing names, probing candidates, and reading selected documents. The adapter facade applies config-owned policy functions and returns typed presets. Config never imports the concrete adapter. Keep capability dependencies explicit and limited to the operations a consumer uses; ordinary function contracts can remain beside their config-owned consumer rather than adding a port that imports config types.

Preserve two distinct algorithms:

1. Discovery enumerates directories, validates names, resolves duplicate names by precedence, and reads only winners.
2. Named loading probes candidates in precedence order and reads the first present candidate. It enumerates available names only to construct the existing missing-name diagnostic; it never parses unrelated preset documents.

Preserve `lstat` semantics: dangling symlinks are present candidates, only `ENOENT` means absence, and other probe/list/read failures remain errors. Do not eagerly load every preset or silently recover from a broken winner. Resolve builtin assets relative to the new adapter module so both source execution and built output find the shipped `presets/` directory.

### Environment and retry defaults

Capture the OS home-directory fallback with the existing process invocation inputs and pass it explicitly into `parseEnvironment`. The parser remains pure and uses normalized `HOME` when present. Preserve telemetry validation/defaults/forwarding and saved credentials filling only unset credential values. Capture inputs without eagerly preparing commands such as help or version.

Move `MAX_STEP_RETRIES` and `RETRY_DELAY_MS` to config-owned defaults and keep `runSettingsFrom` supplying exactly `2` and `5000`. These are maximum retries, not a newly defined total-attempt count. Domain retains `RunSettings`, review-cap comparisons, and independent safety/stopping constants. Add no retry keys to configuration or preset schemas.

### Integration and architectural mismatch

Supply the new operations through existing invocation/container wiring and update preset listing and initialization consumers together with their tests. Callers request loaded configuration, selected presets, or an update; they do not reproduce schemas, filenames, precedence, or read/merge/write sequencing.

The full spec moves preparation to app and construction to a dedicated composition owner. This slice does not complete that larger migration: `with-app.ts` and `app/container.ts` remain the existing integration seams. Record that interim boundary in the implementation PR, while identifying preparation as app policy and process capture/construction as composition responsibility. Do not add an application-wide dependency bag, new container architecture, or config-to-adapter imports. The issue and the targeted spec sections agree on this slice's behavior; the remaining layout difference is explicitly deferred work.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Move the existing config modules wholesale into adapters.** Rejected because this also moves schemas, defaults, precedence, and selection out of their intended owner. Keeping config barrels that re-export adapters would conceal the dependency violation.
2. **Inject a generic filesystem into the existing config modules.** Rejected because it removes direct imports while leaving filesystem sequencing and package discovery mixed with policy. Narrow preset-source operations and pure policy functions expose the actual responsibilities more clearly.
3. **Complete the application API and composition migration now.** Rejected because it expands this bounded refactor into command, container, and resource-lifetime changes. Existing seams can supply the new capabilities without that migration.

## Assumptions

- Existing observable behavior and adjacent specs are the compatibility baseline, including error wording, ordering, and filesystem edge cases.
- Synchronous reads and discovery can remain synchronous; config updates remain asynchronous. Changing concurrency or timing is unnecessary.
- Existing libraries are sufficient: Zod, better-result, Node filesystem operations, and write-file-atomic require no replacement utilities.
- This design response creates no files and runs no implementation verification; the plan specifies those checks for implementation.

## Non-goals

No retry overrides, preset run settings, safety-cap migration, error-class relocation, credential-policy changes, command changes, container replacement, broad application-boundary migration, host agent execution, publication, release tags, or version changes. Preserve init consent, sandbox-only agents, scratch isolation, and tracked-file protections.

## Affected areas

- Config: `load-config.ts`, `write-config.ts`, `presets.ts`, `environment.ts`, config-owned retry defaults, and adjacent specs.
- Adapters: new configuration/preset file operations and their filesystem behavior specs.
- Integration: `cli/with-app.ts`, `cli/commands/presets.ts`, `app/init-sandbox.ts`, the necessary `app/container.ts` wiring, and affected callers/specs.
- Domain: removal of retry-default exports from `settings.ts`; retain resolved settings and business rules.
- Enforcement: `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`, `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, and `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts` as needed for the new boundary.
- Documentation: `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and existing references to moved paths. Describe current ownership in place without adding a new guide or changelog.

# Implementation plan

## Step 1 — Extract configuration file operations and integrate their consumers

Review the applicable house rules and existing config/update tests. Keep config schemas, pure file selection, validation, and merge policy in config; implement read and atomic-update operations under `src/adapters/config/`. Apply the owning schema once at each file boundary and return the existing typed `Result` values.

Wire the operations into configuration preparation and init through narrowly supplied functions using the existing construction seams. Update all affected imports and tests in the same change. Preserve implicit missing-file defaults, explicit missing-file failures, read/JSON/schema diagnostics, permissive object updates, unrelated keys, formatting, and atomic persistence. Keep initialization ordering, symlink refusal, consent, and file-write scope unchanged.

Move disk-dependent cases into adapter specs using temporary directories. Keep disk-free schema/default/merge cases in config specs. Use fakes for failure paths that are unreliable to reproduce with filesystem permissions; follow `setup`, `mock<T>()`, faker-built data, and no-module-mock conventions.

## Step 2 — Separate preset location access from selection policy

Extract concrete location construction, package asset resolution, directory enumeration, `lstat` probing, and file reads into the preset adapter capability. Keep precedence, XDG acceptance, directory deduplication, name validation, shadow selection, schema parsing, missing-name diagnostics, and role replacement in config-owned functions.

Wire discovery, explicit named selection, interactive selection, and preset listing to the new operations. Keep named loading independent of full discovery. Preserve cancellation results and existing output.

Retain and adapt coverage for repository > home > XDG > builtin precedence, repeated directories, invalid filenames, shipped starters, broken higher-precedence winners, dangling links, non-directory ancestors, list/probe/read errors, unrelated malformed presets, and missing-name diagnostics. Test pure selection with supplied data and adapter behavior with temporary directories or narrow fakes. Verify that source and built module locations resolve the same packaged starters and that applying a preset preserves all run settings.

## Step 3 — Make environment parsing independent of process and OS access

Extend invocation capture to supply the home-directory fallback alongside raw environment values. Change `parseEnvironment` and every caller to accept that fallback explicitly; remove `node:os` access from config.

Update environment and preparation specs to supply deterministic inputs. Verify absent and empty `HOME`, explicit `HOME`, relative/absolute XDG behavior through preset resolution, empty-as-unset credentials, environment-over-saved-credential precedence, telemetry validation, defaults, and forwarding.

Preserve operation-specific preparation: repository checks and loading failures remain in their current order, help/version avoid preparation, status retains saved-credential loading without requiring agent credentials or opening a sandbox, and cancellation does not create resources.

## Step 4 — Move retry defaults to config without changing run behavior

Move the two retry-default definitions from `domain/settings.ts` into config and update `runSettingsFrom` and affected references. Keep `RunSettings`, resolved-cap comparisons, and genuine stopping constants in domain.

Verify through resolved-settings behavior that max step retries remains `2` and delay remains `5000` ms. Confirm that retry override keys remain unsupported and preset schemas still reject run settings. Do not replace existing retry execution or introduce new semantics.

## Step 5 — Enforce and document the resulting boundaries

Use the existing Dependency Cruiser configuration and dependency-check fixtures to prevent config from depending on filesystem implementations or concrete adapters, while retaining the ports-only-depend-on-domain restriction. Cover allowed adapter-to-config dependencies and rejected reverse dependencies. Do not add a source scanner; use the requested textual acceptance check separately for process-global access.

Update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` to show config policy/defaults, adapter I/O, process-edge capture, and the actual remaining preparation/composition seams. Search existing guides and source references for moved paths and replace stale references in place. Preserve public behavior documentation where behavior is unchanged.

Prepare the implementation PR explanation of each moved concept's owner and why it belongs there, including the deliberately deferred preparation/container migration. Report any actual disagreement with the spec; do not present deferred target architecture as already implemented.

## Step 6 — Run compatibility and repository verification

Use the Node version pinned in `package.json` (`26.13.0`). Inspect verification scripts before execution to ensure they neither launch agents on the host nor publish to GitHub. Run focused affected specs during implementation, then run every required check from the repository root:

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

Run the acceptance search and confirm it produces no production matches:

```sh
grep -rnE "node:fs|process\.env" src/config --include=*.ts | grep -v spec
```

Also confirm config has no remaining OS home-directory access and domain no longer exports retry defaults. Inspect the final diff for accidental behavior, credential, safety, version, or release changes. Fix failures and rerun the affected checks; report actual verification results and any unresolved blockers without claiming unexecuted checks passed.

1. src/config/presets.ts:15: Remove the JSDoc describing what PresetFiles is; its name and methods already express this. Declaration JSDoc is reserved for non-obvious constraints or rationale.
2. src/config/presets.ts:21: Remove the JSDoc restating what fileFor does; the signature already expresses it.
3. src/config/presets.ts:29: Remove the JSDoc restating what PresetRoots contains; retain the specific XDG constraint on its field.
4. src/adapters/config/preset-files.ts:10: Remove the descriptive JSDoc on presetFilesOnDisk; its name and default parameter already express the implementation and override behavior.

1. src/config/presets.spec.ts:380–382 (also lines 46 and 132–133): Restore an independent assertion of repository > home > XDG > builtin precedence. The replacement tests derive their expected ordering and winners from production's PRESET_SOURCES, weakening the removed explicit home-over-XDG check. With matching presets in home and XDG, swapping those sources would select XDG incorrectly while these tests still pass.
